The gate introduces a minimum of three ACs per capability and explicitly folds smaller capabilities into their neighbours. The specification says count must never decide whether to split. Two independent capabilities with two ACs each therefore remain combined, contrary to the central requirement. The clustering implementation and tests enforce the same unsupported restriction.
findings.suggestion: Remove the minimum group size from the skill, clustering verdicts and authoring rules. Use capability identity and shared evidence to decide whether a split is appropriate.

findings.finding: The JavaScript comment scanner searches for comment delimiters without tracking string literals. For example, `const fixture = "// FR-01.01.AC01";` creates a test binding even though the reference is fixture data. Enough such references can produce a false splittable verdict, contradicting the promised exclusion of string literals.
findings.suggestion: Parse comments with a JavaScript tokenizer, or implement string and template literal handling before recognizing comment delimiters. Add regression cases containing AC references inside quoted strings.

findings.finding: Subtracting hub files from shared-file evidence allows two clusters to be declared splittable even when both import the same source file. The hub test explicitly expects this result. The specification’s stop rule requires no shared tests or files; it does not exempt widely used utilities.
findings.suggestion: Hub filtering may help propose candidate seams, but retain shared files in the evidence and prevent a definitive split recommendation when the stop rule fails.

findings.finding: The two brief outputs are handwritten stand-ins, rather than fresh project-skill runs required by U1. Their clustering check also supplies no test evidence, so it necessarily returns no split regardless of how many unrelated capabilities an FR contains. This does not validate the blocking capability gate.
findings.suggestion: Exercise the project workflow on two briefs and inspect its generated FRs against expected capability boundaries. Include a brief containing independent capabilities with fewer than three ACs each.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The advisory audit is integrated, but the count-based restriction contradicts the specification, and evidence parsing can produce unsupported split recommendations.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
